responsibility: This module provides GCC’s common target-hook infrastructure: the shared, target-sensitive services used by front ends, driver/configuration code, and generic compiler logic that are not specific to any one backend’s instruction selection or machine description. Its core files define the gcc_targetm_common hook interface and its data model, including optimization-level default tables and other common target properties, then supply the standard default hook vector initializers and fallback implementations. Across the common-target and common-targhooks file families, the module covers responsibilities such as target option handling, enumeration of valid target-specific option values, initialization of target flags and optimization defaults, exception-unwind model selection, multilib selection behavior, split-stack and unwind-table related defaults, named-section support, and path canonicalization hooks. In practice, this is the generic target-policy layer that lets GCC expose configurable target behavior outside backend-specific config directories while giving targets a consistent place to override shared option and runtime-policy decisions.
